title: Decentralized Dead Drop — website concepts
artifact_type: Static visual mockups; not implemented webpages

concepts.name: Quiet confidence
concepts.prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup.
Create a polished, high-fidelity website homepage concept image for Decentralized Dead Drop, a private Android text messenger where each community runs its own delivery server. This is a visual design exploration, not a screenshot of a released product. Design the actual flat web page, not a laptop scene or angled presentation.
Product facts to preserve: phones encrypt/decrypt messages; delivery servers hold sealed messages until collected or expired; each community operates an independent server; there is no central messaging service and servers do not federate. No phone number required. The informational website does not handle conversations or user accounts. Android only, early development, not independently security-reviewed. Do not invent audited claims, availability on app stores, metrics, testimonials, prices, blockchain, tokens, cryptocurrency, AI features, calls or media. Message examples must have no read receipts, delivery ticks or typing indicators.
Show a cohesive desktop homepage at high resolution, approximately 1536 x 1152 landscape composition, with navigation, a dramatic hero, substantial product visual, and an intentional second section visible below. All content aligned to a rigorous grid with generous breathing room. No external concept labels, palette swatches, browser toolbars, watermarks, floating brand guideline captions or device photography. Include exactly spelled product name "Decentralized Dead Drop" in the header, permitted as two stacked lines. Nav: "How it works", "Run a server", "Security". Make typography unusually excellent, readable and carefully spaced. Use short real copy rather than lorem ipsum.
Include a legible small status note: "Early development · Not independently audited". Main actions are "Explore the app" and "Run a server". Website copy must emphasize hosting ownership and private conversation, never call the app guaranteed secure. Any product UI shown is an illustrative mobile app, not a web chat offering.

Art direction: a refined, confident evolution of an existing blue-and-cool-grey identity. Paper-white #F5F7FA background, ink #141A24, deep cobalt #264A9A, pale blue #DBE4F8, hairline grey separators. IBM Plex Sans-like humanist sans, oversized condensed display headline, precise small monospace technical labels. Restrained rounded corners, no gradients, no generic feature-card grid.
Layout: understated full-width header with a tiny geometric sealed-drop mark and wordmark at left. Hero is an asymmetric 54/46 split. Left: small "SECURE COMMUNICATION SYSTEMS" eyebrow, very large headline on three lines, exactly "Your people.\nYour server.\nYour conversations." Body exactly "Private messaging, delivered by a server you run." Two clear buttons, followed by the early-development note.
Right: elegant large flat Android app preview within a simple upright charcoal phone bezel, showing "Weekend crew" group with messages "Saturday, same place?", "I'll bring the coffee.", "See you there." Group header has small "Garden server". Calm blue and white chat bubbles. Behind/beside the phone show a compact dark navy panel labelled "YOUR DELIVERY SERVER" containing just sealed packets and "Encrypted message queue"; a simple precise connector connects server and phone. It must be understandable that server holds encrypted content and the phone opens it. Technical panel is a secondary part of the product composition, never dominates.
Second section: white open editorial horizontal band with heading "A simple route. A private conversation." and three numbered compact stages linked by fine rules: "01 Encrypt on your phone", "02 Hold on your server", "03 Open on their phone". Small explanatory line "The server keeps sealed messages only until collected or expired." Bespoke but approachable, trustworthy and practical. Strong negative space, beautiful responsive-web proportions.

Art direction: a memorable, industrial communications instrument translated into excellent contemporary web design. Almost-black charcoal #121513 background, pale warm-white #F2F0E9 typography, vivid safety-orange #F46B38 accents, desaturated sage details. Use a condensed grotesk headline with clean technical monospace microcopy. Precise thin rules, square or barely rounded corners, asymmetric layout, flat dark panels. No neon cyberpunk, padlocks, shield badges, hacker imagery, glowing globes, crypto networks or gradient blobs.
Header: small orange abstract sealed-drop mark beside wordmark, compact right-aligned navigation with a restrained outlined "Run a server" button.
Hero left 55 percent: uppercase micro label "INDEPENDENT BY DESIGN", oversized headline exactly "Own the server.\nKeep the conversation." White main words with "server." in orange. Body exactly "A private messenger for communities that run their own infrastructure." Orange "Run a server" button and text link "Explore the app". Early-development note below in muted readable type.
Hero right 45 percent: a striking custom vector-like technical schematic, elegantly art directed rather than decorative sci-fi. An isometric matte-black physical dead-drop/server box with an orange inset slot; two small sealed orange packets travel along crisp single thin-line paths from a small upright mobile endpoint to the box and from box to another mobile endpoint. Show one single community's server only, no mesh or federated servers. Labels "SENDER", "YOUR SERVER", "RECIPIENT". At the server show only unreadable compact ciphertext glyphs, never actual conversation text. Endpoint message bubbles are simple readable "Meet at six?" and "See you there." The drawing is a conceptual illustration, not app functionality. Tiny unobtrusive caption "Sealed in transit. Opened on your devices."
Second section: broad horizontal rule, left oversize "A delivery server.\nNot a conversation archive." Right three stacked editorial rows numbered 01/02/03: "Encrypted on your phone", "Queued until collected", "Removed when collected or expired". Strong visual hierarchy and considerable breathing room. Looks like premium open engineering, direct and controlled.
